description: A pair of bright-field TEM micrographs of deformed Fe–35% Al placed side by side and recorded over the same area under +g (left) and g(−g, right) two-beam imaging conditions, with a single black scale bar labelled "0.5µm" at the bottom centre bridging the junction between the two panels. Both panels show a mottled grey matrix carrying dark dislocation line contrast: long near-straight or gently bowed lines, plus numerous short dark elongated segments and paired dots. In the right-hand panel many of these short segments are individually flagged with the letter "d", identifying edge dipole segments; comparable dark segments are visible but unlabelled in the left panel. A single heavy black arrow near the lower edge of each panel marks the imaging vector; the two arrows point in roughly opposite directions, consistent with the ±g pair, and features that are strong in one panel appear weak or of inverted contrast in the other — the standard ±g signature used to certify dipoles. No axes, curves or numeric data are printed; the only printed quantity is the 0.5 µm scale bar. The figure demonstrates that a large population of edge dipole segments (and straight superdislocations) exists in the deformed Fe–35% Al structure.
measured_quantities: length scale (µm), given by a 0.5 µm scale bar

observations.observation: The figure consists of two bright-field TEM micrographs of the same area of deformed Fe–35% Al displayed side by side, sharing one scale bar.
A black scale bar labelled "0.5µm" sits at the bottom centre of the figure and spans the junction between the two micrographs.

Both micrographs show dark line contrast (long near-straight or gently bowed dislocations) over a mottled grey matrix, together with numerous short dark elongated segments and paired dot-like features.
In the right-hand micrograph many short dark segments are individually annotated with the letter "d", identifying them as dipole segments; the left-hand micrograph carries no such labels.
Each panel contains one heavy black arrow near its lower edge, and the two arrows point in different, roughly opposite directions, consistent with the two members of a +g/−g imaging pair.
The contrast of individual short segments changes between the two panels (strong in one, weak or inverted in the other), the characteristic ±g behaviour used to identify dislocation dipoles.
No axes, data labels or numeric values are printed anywhere in the figure; the only printed quantity is the 0.5 µm scale bar.
The caption states the two micrographs are a pair of bright field images taken in +g and g (i.e. +g/−g) imaging conditions.
The caption states the sample is deformed Fe–35% Al, with zone axis near [1 1 3] and an imaging vector (marked) of type 1 1 0.
The caption characterises the imaged features as many edge dipole segments.

The citing text states that the dislocations present are superdislocations of the B2 lattice, each constituted by two partials with Burgers vector (1/2) 1 1 1 held close together by the higher APB fault energy.
The citing text states that the large number of dipole segments formed is clearly seen in the pair of images in Fig. 18 imaged under +/− g conditions.
The citing text states that superdislocation motion destroys part of the DO3 order in 28–30% Al alloys, indicated by weak remnant fringes in Fig. 19 (not this figure).

subfigures.description: Bright-field TEM micrograph taken in the +g condition of deformed Fe–35% Al: mottled grey matrix with dark long, near-straight dislocation lines, short dark segments and paired dot contrast; a single heavy black arrow at the lower edge marks the imaging direction; no 'd' labels are applied. The 0.5 µm scale bar begins at this panel's lower right.

Bright-field TEM micrograph of the same area in the opposite (g/−g) condition; many short dark elongated dipole segments are individually labelled with the letter 'd', the dislocation lines show changed/weakened contrast relative to the left panel, and a heavy black arrow near the lower edge points in a different, roughly opposite direction to the left panel's arrow.
